comment_text: WE ARE TAXPAYERS. WE DESERVE CLEAN WATER, NOT A PAIL WITH A FILTER. Every Filipino pays taxes. The tricycle driver, the OFW, the vendor, the employee, the businessman. Even a small share of the budget could build water systems that serve whole cities and provinces for generations. Our own government says about ₱200 billion is needed to solve water scarcity in the country. That's less than 3% of one year's budget. A filter in a bucket is a first-aid kit. It is not a water system. It is not a solution. It is not what taxpayers paid for. We don't need temporary fixes. We need real infrastructure. Mega water systems, desalination plants, and pipelines that bring safe, clean, quality water to every Filipino home, from Luzon to Visayas to Mindanao. This is not about politics. This is about dignity. Clean water is a basic right, not a privilege. Stop the band-aid solutions. We deserve more. comment_text: The 75% score cap directly defeats the legislative intent of the "Preference of Appointment" provision under Section 34 of R.A. 11131. When the law was passed, the legislature intended to elevate and prioritize law enforcement professionals, not penalize them. The mechanism creates a structural barrier through three primary legal and logical contradictions: 1. It Inverts a Privilege into a Mathematical Penalty The legislative intent behind exempting Registered Criminologists from entry exams was to recognize their grueling 4-year degree and their success in passing a national licensure examination. The law treats them as already qualified. The Contradiction: By locking exempted criminologists into a static 75%, the BFP forces them onto a single, integrated ranking list where non-criminologists can easily score 85% to 95% on a basic entry exam. The Result: The statutory "privilege" becomes an automatic disadvantage. Criminologists are pushed down the ranking roster simply because they chose to exercise a right explicitly granted to them by Congress. 2. It Renders "Preference of Appointment" Mathematically ImpossibleSection 34 of R.A. 11131 explicitly states that Registered Criminologists shall enjoy a "preference of appointment" in public safety agencies like the BFP. In legal terms, "preference" means that if all other factors are relatively equal, the professional board passer must be selected first. The Contradiction: The BFP’s recruitment system relies entirely on a sequential, top-to-bottom numerical ranking based on a composite score (QWE + Physical Agility Test + Panel Interview). The Result: Because the 75% cap severely drags down a criminologist's total composite score, they are systematically barred from reaching the top tiers of the list. You cannot give "preference" to a criminologist if the scoring system ensures they never make it to the final quota selection pool. 3. It Forces a Forfeiture of Statutory Rights (The Waiver Dilemma)To bypass the 75% disadvantage and remain competitive, BFP guidelines pressure Registered Criminologists to sign a waiver, forfeit their legal exemption, and take the standard Qualifying Written Examination (QWE). The Contradiction: An administrative policy or memorandum circular cannot force an individual to surrender a right granted by national statutory law just to achieve basic fairness. The Result: If a criminologist must give up their statutory right (the exemption) just to survive the ranking process, then the law is rendered toothless and effectively nullified by the Bureau's internal recruitment mechanics.

comment_text: The implementation of BFP Memorandum Circular No. 2026-014 (dated July 07, 2026), Paragraph V (Guidelines), Letter J, concerning the selection process for Fire Officer 1 (FO1) dictates that applicant advancement to subsequent evaluation stages, specifically the Physical Agility Test (PAT), shall be strictly contingent upon score rankings and arbitrary candidate pool cut-offs established through a preliminary Digital Examination. By subjecting Registered Criminologists to a score-based written elimination test as a prerequisite for recruitment advancement, the Bureau of Fire Protection effectively conditions, modifies, and nullifies an express statutory privilege granted by the Congress of the Philippines under Section 34, Article V of Republic Act No. 11131 (The Philippine Criminology Profession Act of 2018). This establishes that the agency's enforcement of an exclusionary written test cut-off against statutory eligibles constitutes an ultra vires act, violates the Equal Protection Clause, transgresses statutory construction principles, and abuses administrative discretion. It is a fundamental principle of administrative law that executive agencies derive their rule-making power strictly from delegated legislative authority. An administrative issuance, such as a Memorandum Circular, occupies a subordinate position in the hierarchy of legal norms and must at all times conform to the terms, standards, and intent of the governing statute. In settled Philippine jurisprudence (Smart Communications v. NTC, G.R. No. 151908), the Supreme Court has consistently held that administrative regulations cannot extend, restrict, modify, or supplant acts of Congress. When a direct conflict arises between a statute enacted by the Legislature and a rule promulgated by an executive bureau, the statute unequivocally prevails. By instituting an administrative filter that excludes statutory eligibles from recruitment consideration, the Bureau of Fire Protection acts ultra vires and exceeds its statutory jurisdiction. Republic Act No. 11131 explicitly establishes the scope of privileges conferred upon licensed criminologists. Section 34, Article V expressly provides that Registered Criminologists shall be exempt from taking any other entrance or qualifying government or civil service examinations and shall be deemed civil service eligible for uniformed positions, including Firefighter and Fire Marshal. Under the statutory construction canon of verba legis (the plain meaning rule), when the language of the law is clear, explicit, and unambiguous, it must be applied as written without interpretation or extrapolation. Congress granted this absolute exemption because passing the national licensure examination administered by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) already confirms professional competency for law enforcement and public safety roles. The agency possesses no legal discretion to re-test or filter these individuals through an administrative written examination. The argument that the Digital Examination is merely an "internal screening or ranking tool" rather than an "entrance exam" constitutes an impermissible semantic evasion. Where a written examination score operates as an indispensable threshold barrier such that failing or falling below a ranking cut-off results in immediate disqualification prior to physical, medical, and psychological evaluations that examination functions in fact and in law as a qualifying screening examination. Settled legal principles dictate that an administrative authority cannot accomplish indirectly what it is expressly prohibited from doing directly. Utilizing an internal scoring metric to bar licensed criminologists from advancing to physical agility testing constitutes a constructive revocation of their statutory exemption, rendering the statutory grant illusory and ineffective. The enforcement of BFP Memorandum Circular No. 2026-014 violates the Equal Protection Clause guaranteed under Article III, Sec
